hypothesis: Linked cycle endpoints, complete competitors, shortest exits and cross-branch targets can repair traps; exact solved-preserving axis equivariance can make those repairs transfer across presentations without identifying state Qs.
architecture: Same 192->256->256->128 sigmoid MLP, shared across six solved-preserving presentations. Align each 128D output by 21 regular six-channel coordinate permutations plus two invariant channels, then average. Final distance is the unchanged Linf norm. Six forwards per state; floating-point tolerance applies. Plain checkpoint weights initialize the projection, but its initial predictions change and are evaluated separately. No manually assigned distance coordinates.
split: Select frozen cycle monitors before training and protect their endpoints and complete stars. Close this mask and the historical fixed-goal mask under all six axis symmetries. Reject entire cycle packs containing a protected state. Apply the same closed mask to both control arms and all base, path, arbitrary-goal and cycle labels. Pretraining may have seen monitor relations; this measures continuation transfer and retention, not never-seen relations.
selection: Fixed small update budget, fresh Adam for all conditions, same initial weights and matched base RNG streams. Cycle conditions add labels and compute. Report before/after per condition, including the changed projection initialization. No test-based checkpoint choice or automatic longer run. Detailed runtime output stays outside Git.
